distractors.reason: 'Big' describes physical size. We say 'heavy workload', not 'big workload', for an amount of work.
'Strong' describes force, taste or feelings. It does not describe an amount of work.
'Thick' describes objects with a large distance between two surfaces, such as thick walls. It is never used for work.

example_sentence: I have a ___ workload this month, so I cannot take new projects.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes a veces traducen literalmente 'grande' y dicen 'big workload' en vez del correcto 'heavy workload'.
explanation: In English, 'heavy' is used for things that are hard to carry or handle, and also for large amounts of pressure or responsibility, such as heavy rain, heavy traffic and heavy workload.

related_collocations.example: We have a tight deadline for this report.
She was promoted to senior manager last year.
The annual report will be published in March.

memory_tip: HEAVY = a lot of weight, pressure or responsibility (heavy workload, heavy rain) | BIG = physical size (big house, big dog)
